macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Nasdaq plunges 2.6% as AI spending concerns hit tech stocks
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6%, its steepest decline in months, while the S&P 500 dropped 1.2% for its worst session since July. The Dow edged up less than 0.1% as defensive sectors outperformed technology shares.[1][2]

items.title: Treasury yields post biggest decline since 2023
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 19–20 basis points to roughly 4.95%, as investors sought safety amid the technology selloff and concerns that an AI investment pullback could weaken economic growth.[3][4]

items.title: Oil rises above $111 amid Middle East supply risks
items.summary: Brent crude climbed above $111 a barrel after fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and heightened concerns about potential U.S.-Iran hostilities disrupting regional oil supplies.[5][6]

items.title: Markets increase bets that Fed will hold rates next week
items.summary: Fed-funds futures put the probability of no rate change at about 93%, up from 85% previously, as resilient labor-market data and higher oil prices reinforced inflation concerns.[2][7]

items.title: South Korea central bank pauses rate increases
items.summary: The Bank of Korea held its policy rate steady after two consecutive increases, citing easing inflation while inflation remained above target.[1]

items.title: Meta and Tesla earnings intensify AI and valuation concerns
items.summary: Meta shares fell after the company raised its projected artificial-intelligence spending, while Tesla reported lower quarterly profits and adjusted its capital-spending forecast. The mixed results renewed concerns about the scale and payoff of AI investment.[8][10]

items.title: Western Digital and Deckers shares fall after earnings updates
items.summary: Western Digital reversed initial post-earnings gains after warning about higher input costs and rising capital expenditure. Deckers fell more than 7% after missing revenue expectations and issuing below-consensus guidance.[2]

items.title: U.S. jobless claims remain near historic lows
items.summary: Initial unemployment claims fell to 194,000 for the week ended October 17 from a revised 200,000, signaling continued labor-market resilience as markets assess the Federal Reserve’s inflation outlook.[7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies fall in broad risk-off sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 3.4%–4.1% below $82,000 as crypto markets tracked losses in technology equities amid AI-spending concerns, higher oil prices and geopolitical tensions. Ethereum fell roughly 3.5%–4.4%, while XRP, Solana and other major altcoins also declined; crypto futures liquidations reached approximately $441 million–$474 million.[1][2][6]
items.source: FXStreet / The Block / Reuters via Marketscreener

items.title: Russia proposes regulated access to bitcoin, ether and USDT
items.summary: Russia’s central bank reportedly proposed allowing bitcoin, ether and USDT to trade on regulated exchanges while limiting annual crypto purchases by non-qualified investors to 300,000 rubles per intermediary.[3]

items.title: CFTC investigates prediction-market incentive programs
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is examining incentive programs used by prediction markets amid concerns about potentially misleading promotion.[4]

items.title: Coinbase expands crypto-collateralized lending
items.summary: Coinbase added Hyperliquid’s HYPE and Zcash’s ZEC as collateral options for its crypto-backed lending service, allowing eligible users to borrow up to $100,000 without selling their assets.[4]

items.title: Irish regulator penalizes Coinbase Ireland
items.summary: Ireland’s central bank reportedly fined Coinbase Ireland $3.6 million over fund-safeguarding issues.[9]

items.title: Hong Kong regulator flags BTCC as suspicious platform
items.summary: Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission added BTCC to its list of suspicious virtual-asset trading platforms.[10]

items.title: Visa reportedly explores $2.5 billion Fireblocks acquisition
items.summary: Visa is reportedly in talks to acquire crypto-custody infrastructure provider Fireblocks for approximately $2.5 billion, though the discussions have not been confirmed and terms remain undisclosed.[10]

items.title: Circle targets expansion into emerging markets
items.summary: Circle is pursuing expansion into about 40 emerging and developing countries as it seeks to broaden stablecoin adoption, supported by its reported acquisition of Tazapay and strategic investment from Binance.[8]

items.title: Kazakhstan considers gas-powered crypto mining rules
items.summary: Kazakhstan is drafting rules that could permit cryptocurrency mining using natural gas currently flared at oil fields, potentially involving as many as 60 fields.[4]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI broadly launches Decisions API model
items.summary: OpenAI has made its Decisions API model available to all customers, expanding competition in fast, low-cost AI systems designed to select among options and provide confidence scores. The company says the model can reduce response latency to roughly 100–180 milliseconds and supports voice and visual inputs.[1]

items.title: Chinese companies announce new decision and multimodal models
items.summary: A technology-news roundup reports releases and availability developments involving iFlytek’s Spark X2.6 multimodal model and Ant Digital’s LingDT-Decision-1.0, which reportedly cuts token consumption by more than 90%. The roundup also says DeepSeek and MiniMax have completed open-source and overseas licensing work.[2]

items.title: NSF renews two AI institutes with $38.4 million
items.summary: The U.S. National Science Foundation awarded $20 million to renew the AI Institute for Advances in Optimization and $18.4 million to renew the AI Institute for Adult Learning and Online Education, supporting both programs through new five-year periods.[3]

items.title: AI-assisted discovery helps identify critical PHP vulnerabilities
items.summary: Security teams are rushing to patch vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language used by a large share of websites. The incident highlights both the defensive potential of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and the risk that similar capabilities could accelerate cyberattacks.[4]

items.title: Meta faces continued scrutiny over AI training and news websites
items.summary: Meta changed business terms that appeared to permit unrestricted AI training on news websites, but legal experts told The Verge that the revisions may not resolve publishers’ concerns about data scraping and model training rights.[9]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA cuts about 400 jobs and closes BioWare
items.summary: Electronic Arts is cutting roughly 3% of its workforce, closing BioWare, and reportedly canceling a Mass Effect project as it refocuses on selected franchises.[2][3]

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches amid major competition
items.summary: Activision is positioning Modern Warfare 4 as a return to form, with the latest Call of Duty installment facing heightened expectations and competition from major releases including Grand Theft Auto VI.[1]

items.title: PEGI raises ratings for games with paid random items
items.summary: PEGI has begun applying tougher ratings to games featuring loot boxes and similar randomized paid rewards. EA Sports FC 27, previously rated PEGI 3, has reportedly been reassigned PEGI 16 with a paid-random-items descriptor.[6]

items.title: Marvel’s Wolverine tops US September game sales
items.summary: Marvel’s Wolverine led US game sales in September and recorded the strongest monthly dollar sales for a Sony-published title since Helldivers 2. PlayStation 5 also led the month in hardware sales.[4]

items.title: EA pauses The Sims Project Lotus during restructuring
items.summary: EA has reportedly paused development of Project Lotus, a second Sims project, while restructuring other development plans, including projects linked to Mass Effect, Skate, Respawn, and DICE.[5]
